channel.title: Carat Capital — The Trade Paper of the Jewelry World
channel.description: Prices, intelligence and analysis from every desk of the stone trade: diamonds, gold and metals, gemstones, watches, auctions, retail and technology.

item.title: Oura's $44 top IPO price values a ring at $14.1bn
item.description: The prospectus filed with the SEC on 21 September puts 50 million shares on sale, 73% of them from existing holders. Eli Lilly and Dragoneer have signalled $400m of interest.

item.title: GJEPC puts FY2025-26 exports at $27.72bn, members at 10,910
item.description: The council's 60th annual meeting sat at the Bharat Diamond Bourse on 23 September. Chairman Kirit Bhansali counted four free trade agreements signed in the year, with the UK, EU, Oman and New Zealand.

item.title: Boko ties diamond demand to 20,000 Okavango community members
item.description: Botswana's president spoke in New York on 23 September at a De Beers and National Geographic event. He announced a second phase for Okavango Eternal, the partnership now in year five of ten.

item.title: Gold rises $42.10 to $4,296.60 after Thursday's four-metal fall
item.description: Silver gained 1.45% and platinum 0.92% on the Kitco bid at 06:07 ET, against Thursday's marks. London's newest fixes, all dated 24 September, still point the other way.

item.title: Mastercard forecasts 6% US holiday growth, online up 11%
item.description: In-store sales are put at 3.6% for 1 November to 24 December, and Mastercard says higher prices account for about half the rise. It names energy costs and AI-driven demand.

item.title: Richard Mille takes GB1 timekeeping for the 38th America's Cup
item.description: The British challenger races the second preliminary regatta at Naples from 24 to 27 September, and will launch a reconfigured AC75 by the end of 2026. No terms were disclosed.

item.title: Gold sheds $61.60 to $4,254.50, silver and platinum fall further
item.description: Silver lost 2.45% and platinum 2.41% on the Kitco bid at 06:04 ET, against Wednesday's marks. London's newest fixes, dated 23 September, moved the same way on all four metals.

item.title: Sotheby's Hong Kong jewellery sale makes HK$58.8m, 294 lots offered
item.description: A 44.90-carat Ceylon sapphire pendant led at HK$1,800,000, 2.57 times its HK$700,000 high estimate. The house's own page carries no sale total; that figure is Rapaport's.

item.title: Gold $1,300 below January's high changes what jewellers make
item.description: Goldman Sachs forecasts $4,900 an ounce by year end and ING $4,600, JCK reports. McKinsey's ConsumerWise survey found 43% of consumers expect to spend less on jewellery over the next three months.

item.title: AGTA takes 12.5% gemstone tariff to Bangkok trade talks
item.description: Thai finished jewellery entering the United States carries combined duties of 17.5% to 19.5%, the association says. It met Thailand's vice minister for commerce and passed the discussion to the US Trade Representative.

item.title: Census puts August retail sales at $773.9bn, up 1.2%
item.description: The Census Bureau's advance estimate, released 16 September, carries a margin of 0.4 points on the monthly change and no jewellery line. Sales were 6.0% above August 2025.

item.title: Sotheby's sells a Cartier Cheich for HK$26.52m in Hong Kong
item.description: The one-off white-gold prize watch carried a HK$8.0m to HK$40m estimate. Two trade accounts convert the same Hong Kong dollar result differently, at US$3.38m and US$3,413,124.

item.title: Elmwood's puts a £2m high estimate on an 8.03-carat blue
item.description: The pear-shaped Fancy Light Blue comes from a Glasgow collector and carries a £1.5m low estimate. The house says only two blue diamonds above eight carats have been offered at UK auction before, in 1865 and 2008.

item.title: China's gold imports top 1,000 tonnes in eight months
item.description: Customs data put January to August above the roughly 886 tonnes imported in all of 2025, at a cost near US$158.8bn. Chinese gold ETFs added about 11 tonnes in August to 293 tonnes.

item.title: De Beers cuts Scope 1 and 2 emissions 14% since 2021
item.description: The 2025 report books US$70m committed to Botswana's Diamonds for Development Fund and 375,000 acres under conservation management. Five million rough stones have now been scanned on Tracr.

item.title: Natural Diamond Council renames itself The Diamond Collective
item.description: The trade's natural-diamond marketing body dropped the qualifier from its name on 22 September, with a new logo and a stated goal of creating desire. Its first fashion partnership is promised for 2027.

item.title: India's gold imports fall 45% to US$2.3bn as ETFs reach 121.3t
item.description: Domestic prices traded below import parity through August, and discounts widened from US$34 an ounce in July to US$51. Indian gold ETFs took INR25.97bn, an inflow up 67% on the month.

item.title: RAPI restates all five daily points read a day earlier
item.description: The one-carat series read on 21 September and again on 22 September differs at every overlapping date, by between 12 and 27 cents. The level is barely changed; the dating of a quote is not.

item.title: Thailand's gold exports fall 59.22% in July to US$411.04m
item.description: Gem and jewellery exports excluding gold slipped 6.36% to US$737.93m, the first monthly fall after four straight gains. Seven-month exports excluding gold still run 9.87% ahead at US$8,981.12m.

item.title: Gold falls $14.50 to $4,333.70 with all four metals lower
item.description: Silver gave up 0.92% and palladium 0.78% against Monday's marks on Kitco's bid. Gold's overnight range ran from $4,290.70 to $4,376.90, a span of $86.20.

item.title: RAPI's 1-carat rises to $3,916.19 across five sessions
item.description: The index published a new point on each of 17, 18, 19 and 20 September, a rise of $4.28 from the 16th. IDEX's broad one-carat driver averaged $3,051.17 on the same morning, 22.1% below the narrow benchmark.

item.title: De Beers and Shanghai's bourse meet on natural-diamond value
item.description: The Natural Diamond Council and the Diamond Federation of Hong Kong convened the session on 17 September, during Jewellery & Gem World. The World Federation of Diamond Bourses and De Beers sat on the panel; no figures were released.

item.title: Gold opens the week $28.80 lower at $4,348.20 an ounce
item.description: Silver added half a cent, platinum lost a dollar and palladium lost a dollar. The board's overnight range on gold ran from $4,339.30 to $4,384.30, a swing of $45.

item.title: Rings.com puts the lab-grown 1-carat median back at $571
item.description: The September edition read 251,098 listings at seven US retailers on 17 September. Ritani raised its one-carat asking median 26% while Brilliant Earth cut its 1.5-carat cell 32%.

item.title: ICBC sets gold margin at 190%, forced-sale line at 170%
item.description: More than 10 Chinese banks have shut or tightened personal access to Shanghai Gold Exchange metals trading this year. The count stood at 6 on 9 September; Pudong Development closes its channel on 25 September.

item.title: 300kg of gold clears Sanya airport from Singapore
item.description: The consignment transited Guangzhou and moved into the Shanghai Gold Exchange's Sanya warehouse. Customs ran advance declaration, air-to-air transit and apron collection as one procedure, which Sanya Daily reports as a first at the port.

item.title: DGFT drops the RCMC requirement on exports under ₹3 lakh
item.description: Notification 36/2026-27 amends paragraph 2.57 of the Foreign Trade Policy 2023, effective 15 September. Consignments up to USD 3,000 were 43% of India's shipping bills and 0.86% of export value from 2021-22 to 2025-26.

item.title: India's polished exports fall 4.93% in value, rise 3.23% in carats
item.description: Total gem and jewellery exports reached $2.30 billion in August, up 3.14% year on year on the council's figures. Studded gold jewellery added 51.22% to $642.85 million.

item.title: DGCX hands its trading and clearing engine to TCS
item.description: Tata Consultancy Services will supply BaNCS for central counterparty clearing and trading, and Quartz for surveillance and connectivity. TCS shares rose 5.19% to ₹2,315 on the National Stock Exchange on 15 September.

item.title: SCS retires SCS-007, the gemstone standard no miner adopted
item.description: The scheme covered natural and laboratory-grown diamonds, emeralds, rubies and sapphires, and ended on 1 September. Companies already certified may use their certificates until expiry, but SCS will no longer audit or maintain the standard.
